reason: Funiculate means the ovule is borne on a funicle, PO:0020006 (synonym funiculus). In 'short-funiculate', 'short' is decreased length (PATO_0000574) of the funicle.
Sub- plus angular (PATO_0001977, synonym angulate) with value_qualifier 'sub'. The French 'subanguleux' is the same word.
A rendering of French 'fauve' (tawny, fulvous), a light yellowish- to orange-brown. PATO has no tawny; yellow brown is the nearest colour value.

Anthers and fruits ending abruptly in a very short point ('apex with extremely short tip') = a minute mucro. PATO has 'apiculate' only as a synonym of the attribute PATO:0000944 sharpness, which is not a value.
Hemi-isophyllous = the leaves of a pair or rank nearly equal: equal (FLOPO:0991102) with value_qualifier 'nearly'. No term for isophylly or anisophylly exists, and the degree is vague.

label: paracytic
definition: A spatial pattern quality inhering in a stomatal complex by virtue of each guard cell being flanked by one or more subsidiary cells whose long axes are parallel to the long axis of the guard cells. NOTE: PATO has no stomatal types; tetracytic, anisocytic, anomocytic and diacytic are siblings. Bearer stomatal complex PO:0002000.
reason: A standard stomatal type in leaf anatomy with no PATO or FLOPO term; the floras pair it with tetracytic.
Coniform = cone-shaped, which is PATO:0002021 conical (EXACT synonym cone-shaped).
'Stipules falling', 'soon falling' = shed early (deciduous, caducous). Same as the NCVC rule 'stipule deciduous (generic)'. 'Soon' is the timing and is not kept.

target: new: two values of one bearer (congested PATO_0001836 and cymose, which has no term)
reason: Not a continuum: the inflorescence is a cyme and its flowers are crowded, so both hold. Latin 'congesto-cymosae'. Cymose needs its own decision, like raceme-like and thyrse-like.
Calyculate = with a calyculus, an outer series of small bracts at the base of the involucre; PO lists calyculus as a synonym of epicalyx PO:0009063. Not calyculate = calyculus absent.
A prow tip (Poaceae) is a boat-shaped blade apex, where the keel and the incurved margins meet like the bow of a boat. Annotate scaphoid on leaf apex PO:0020137.
Like ovate-lanceolate: an indumentum between tomentose (PATO_0002341) and pubescent (PATO_0000455). The French 'tomenteux-pubescent' is the same.
A transcription of oblong-elliptic with the hyphen lost: a continuum between oblong (PATO_0000946) and elliptic (PATO_0000947).

target: new: part of the bearer (corolla throat, no PO or FLOPO class; nearest corolla tube FLOPO_0985018) + length (PATO_0000122)
reason: Not a quality word: a measurement (docs/odp/02) of the throat, the widened part of the corolla between tube and lobes. Like thin-walled, it needs the part as the bearer.
The bract base forms a sheath round the axis; 'short' is the length of that sheath, a part of the bearer, and is not kept by this rule.
Finely wrinkled across the axis. FLOPO has no rugulose term, so this maps to rugose. 'Cross' (transverse) is the direction of the wrinkles and is not kept.

label: incumbent
definition: A positional quality inhering in the cotyledons of a curved embryo by virtue of the radicle lying against the back of one cotyledon. NOTE: Sibling of accumbent, where the radicle lies against the edges of the cotyledons (Brassicaceae). 'Incombant' is the French spelling.
reason: A diagnostic embryo character in Brassicaceae and Cleomaceae with no PATO or FLOPO term.
Sappy stems (as in Impatiens) are soft and full of watery sap, which is the succulent quality. PATO_0002351 fleshy would be the fallback.
Bacterial leaf nodules that are dot-shaped = small and point-like, which is PATO:0001366 punctiform.
A base that is stipe-like = narrowed into a stalk, i.e. borne on a stipe. Same reading as the rule for 'stalked'.
The French 'en relief' (veins, network of veins) = standing above the surface: PATO:0001369 raised, the opposite of the rule impressed = sunken.
A count of veins with a vague number, like few-flowered. The counted part is vascular bundle PO:0005020 (synonym vein).
'Plants bulbose' = plants with a bulb. 'Hairs with bulbose base' is a different sense (PATO_0002210 bulbous) and is excluded by the bearer constraint.
Sub- plus oblong (PATO_0000946) with value_qualifier 'sub', as for suborbicular.
Sub- plus revolute (PATO_0001963) with value_qualifier 'sub': margins slightly rolled under.
Flat-headed (flat-topped) panicles are described by the flora itself as compound corymbs, i.e. corymb-like in outline.

Says the stem or caudex does not keep the old leaf bases after the leaves fall. Absence of remaining leaf bases on the older stem is the content. The ELK check must confirm that the leaves themselves are not taken to lack a base.
The French form of infundibuliform, already mapped to funnel-shaped (rule C218).

target: new: two values of one bearer (ciliate margin, no term, and strigose FLOPO:0991086 on the marginal hairs)
reason: Not a continuum: the margin is fringed with hairs that are stiff and appressed, so both hold. Ciliate needs its own term; PATO:0001408 ciliated is about cilia on cells.
It negates locellate (anther thecae divided into small chambers by cross-walls), which has no PATO or FLOPO term and no PO part for the locellus. Decide the positive word first.
